rationale: A is much more decision-useful: it distinguishes among live alternatives, gives concrete implementation guidance, includes measurable KPIs, forecasts with ranges, identifies failure modes, and specifies review triggers and fallback actions. Its quantitative estimates may be rough, but they materially help compare options and plan monitoring. B gives a sensible hybrid recommendation and one useful operating rule, but it is lighter on uncertainty, lacks quantitative support, and does less to help a careful decision-maker choose among variants or know when to change course.
